newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cuba 6-6.5 mln T sugar output feasible goal - ISO.
newsitem.headline: Cuba 6-6.5 mln T sugar output feasible goal - ISO.

text.p: A possible feasible goal for Cuban sugar authorities is to produce between six million and 6.5 million tonnes per year, the head of the economics and statistics division of the International Sugar Organisation said here Wednesday.

"That Cuba will recover is not in doubt. It is an economic necessity for the island whatever the time frame and future political developments. The question is the optimum level. A lean, efficient industry producing six million to 6.5 million tonnes may be a feasible goal," Tony Hannah said.
Speaking to the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference, Hannah said Cuba has already implemented a recovery program involving foreign investment, mainly in inputs such as fertilizer.

"This resulted in an improvement of more than one million tonnes in 1996 to a production of 4.5 million tonnes," Hannah said, adding that output in 1990 had been 8.44 million tonnes. "By 1995, it had fallen to 3.26 million tonnes, a fall of no less than 5.18 million tonnes, or 61 percent," he added.
Hannah said two decades earlier that would have been enough to trigger a price boom but he said three factors absorbed the shock of the Cuban production decline.

One, he said, was the fall in supply was partly balanced by a fall in demand from the former Soviet Union. Another was the domination of the import market by high price elasticity developing countries and the third was that potential supply problems were eased by rapid expansions of production and exports in Brazil, Australia and Thailand.
